Method: SHMEM intra-host transport (WP-SHMEM, same-host auto-select + UDP fallback)
Artifact: src/dds-xport/shmem.lisp; src/dds-disc/{dataplane,disc}.lisp; src/dds-rtps/discovery.lisp; dds-tests shmem-{ring-init,lane-claim,enqueue,drain,drain-resource-guard,locator-wire,transport,receiver-thread,stress,end-to-end}; scripts/shmem-roundtrip.sh (make shmem-xproc); src/dds-bench/ (make bench-shmem)
Notes: WP-SHMEM Task F-series DONE 2026-06-14 (ADR 0013). Same-host intra-host transport delivering the IDENTICAL serialized RTPS datagrams through a POSIX mmap ring instead of UDP; engine UNTOUCHED (constructs the frozen dds.xport:transport record; feeds the same %handle-datagram). Segment per receiver = [header | pthread PROCESS_SHARED mutex+cond+stop+parked notify block | K per-sender SPSC lanes]; lane claim is MUTEX-GUARDED (no foreign-SAP CAS -> SBCL+Clasp full parity at that layer); steady-state enqueue/drain are lock-free aligned-u64 store/load + a REAL release/acquire fence; CONDITIONAL (parked-flag, Dekker StoreLoad) wakeup so a busy receiver is not futex-signalled per message; pshared mutex/cond NOT named semaphores (sem_open undrivable from the Lisp runtime on macOS arm64). Selection (dds.disc): auto-routes same-host USER DATA over SHMEM iff the remote shares this node's host-uuid (MD5 of hostname, SPDP-advertised) AND advertised a SHMEM Locator_t (vendor kind 0x47420001) + PID_SHMEM_HOST_UUID (vendor 0x8040); the resolved dest is CACHED per remote (0 per-datagram alloc) and invalidated on re-discovery/lease-out. UDP IS THE FALLBACK and carries ALL discovery/metatraffic/HEARTBEAT/ACKNACK + every non-SHMEM case; a peer that does not understand the SHMEM kind ignores it (fail-open) and matches over UDP; cross-vendor SHMEM out of scope (no standard RTPS SHMEM wire format). Ring is an UNTRUSTED parser surface — every len/offset bounds-checked vs lane extents even at (safety 0) (NFR-SEC-POSTURE); lane/ring-full -> reject -> UDP fallback for that datagram, NEVER a GC-heap fallback (reliable sample repairs via HEARTBEAT/ACKNACK). Hot-path: send stays slot-read + funcall (FR-XPORT-5), enqueue is raw SAP writes, 0 bytes/sample steady-state on the SHMEM send path (gate-hotpath + make mem cover it; the gated XCDR codec is already 0-alloc). TESTS (all green SBCL): shmem-ring-init/lane-claim/enqueue/drain/drain-resource-guard (ring unit), shmem-locator-wire (locator codec), shmem-transport/receiver-thread (transport + threaded receiver loopback), shmem-end-to-end (in-process disc-layer integration over SHMEM), shmem-stress (4 senders x 5000 distinct -> exactly 20000 delivered, no loss/corruption/deadlock), the ring-record-parser fuzz (make fuzz: malformed len, wrap-sentinel edge, oversized record), make shmem-xproc (REAL 2-process cross-image round-trip — the proof loopback within one image cannot give), run-bench-shmem (make bench-shmem). BENCH (bench/report/2026-06-14-wp-shmem.md, SBCL/macOS Apple M5): LATENCY WIN 1.35x-1.94x lower one-way p50 vs UDP loopback (largest for small payloads), p99 comparable-to-better, lower max tail; reliable END-TO-END samples/s is HEARTBEAT/ACKNACK-handshake + poll-granularity bound (NOT SHMEM-bound — UDP baseline itself swings ~10x run-to-run), a direct send-path micro-bench isolates the conditional-wakeup at ~1.4x-1.8x raw send throughput; SHMEM bytes/sample now at the UDP baseline (the per-datagram make-shmem-locator + subseq removed by the dest-cache). NFR-PORT: SBCL has FULL SHMEM on every platform; Clasp/macOS-arm64 -> UDP (shm_open variadic mode_t mispass, shm-attach-by-name-reliable-p NIL, *shmem-enabled* defaults NIL there, SHMEM tests pass-skip cleanly); Clasp/Linux SHMEM EXPECTED via register-varargs ABI, PENDING verification on a Linux host; AllegroCL absent (existing NFR-PORT gap). Remaining transport follow-up: lock-free-MPSC ring + Linux futex fast-path (deferred, measured); Zero-Copy-over-SHMEM (FR-PF-3) reuses this segment + notification machinery. 165 tests green SBCL; gate-types (1043 defuns) + gate-hotpath + fuzz + mem green.

Method: READER_DATA_LIFECYCLE autopurge of NOT_ALIVE instances (DDS 1.4 §2.2.3.22)
Notes: READER_DATA_LIFECYCLE (DDS 1.4 §2.2.3.22): a DataReader purges all internal information + untaken samples for a NOT_ALIVE instance after a configurable delay — autopurge_disposed_samples_delay after it became NOT_ALIVE_DISPOSED, autopurge_nowriter_samples_delay after it became NOT_ALIVE_NO_WRITERS. QoS: two qos-duration slots autopurge-nowriter-samples-delay + autopurge-disposed-samples-delay on dds.qos:qos + make-reader-qos, BOTH default DURATION_INFINITE (the common default is a NO-OP: nothing is ever purged); reader-local, NOT advertised in SEDP, NOT RxO-checked (qos-rxo-compatible unchanged). The instance-rec gains not-alive-since (an internal-time stamp, %lease-now, or nil while ALIVE): set on every ALIVE->NOT_ALIVE transition (%note-not-alive-since, the single stamping point, called from %drain-one-lifecycle for dispose/no-writers AND %on-writer-vanished), cleared on revival to ALIVE (%reader-revive-instance). %autopurge-sweep runs on the DCPS announce cadence (spin, beside %writer-liveliness-sweep, over %participant-readers): for each NOT_ALIVE instance-rec it picks the applicable delay (disposed -> autopurge_disposed_samples_delay; no-writers -> autopurge_nowriter_samples_delay) and, when that delay is finite (not DURATION_INFINITE) AND now-not-alive-since >= the delay (Duration_t->internal-units via %lease-internal-units, the same lease arithmetic the liveliness sweep uses, DRY), PURGES the instance — %autopurge-purge-instance removes its untaken cached samples from dr-cache, its instance-rec from dr-instance-recs (state/gen-counts/writers-set/owner pointer), and its dr-instances view-state entry — so a later sample for the same key starts a brand-new ALIVE instance (view-state NEW, generation counts reset 0). The per-writer dr-drained high-water is intentionally left intact (keyed by writer GUID not instance, RTPS 2.5 §8.3.5.4 — suppresses a replayed lower SN while a fresh higher-SN sample still drains). Mutates dr-cache + instance-recs on the user/spin thread only (the dr-cache owner thread), never the receiver thread (S2 lock discipline). Test dcps-autopurge (deterministic offline injection — stage data + dispose/unregister in the engine SN maps, %drain, BACKDATE not-alive-since past the delay, run %autopurge-sweep, no UDP/no real wait): (a) DEFAULT both-INFINITE never purges a disposed instance (instance-rec + cached samples stay); (b) finite disposed delay -> WITHIN the delay not purged, PAST the delay the instance-rec + cached samples + view-state entry are gone and a new sample for the same key is a FRESH ALIVE instance (view NEW, disposed_generation_count 0); (c) same via the no-writers path under a finite autopurge_nowriter_samples_delay; (d) a disposed-delay reader does NOT purge a NOT_ALIVE_NO_WRITERS instance and a still-ALIVE instance is NEVER purged. REGRESSION: default-INFINITE = no behaviour change — all instance-lifecycle (dcps-instance-state, dcps-no-writers, dcps-disposed-sticky, dcps-drain-sn-order, dcps-autodispose-reader/writer, dcps-writer-unmatch) + ownership + data-plane/SEDP/DCPS tests green. 136 tests green SBCL+Clasp; gate-types + gate-hotpath green.

Method: TX in the writer's offered representation — XCDR1-LE byte-exact + TX->RX round-trip (DDS-XTypes 1.3 §7.6.3.1.1; §7.6.3.1.2 Table 60)
Notes: WP-DATA-REPRESENTATION step 2 (FlatData TX-transcode = R6). The writer serializes+sends in (first (qos-data-representation writer-qos)): :xcdr2 -> PLAIN_CDR2_LE (0x0007, the default, byte-identical existing wire), :xcdr1 -> PLAIN_CDR_LE (0x0001). The codec alignment mode AND the encapsulation id are both rep-derived in one place (%rep->codec); the serialized-size path honours the mode (XCDR1 8-byte alignment >= XCDR2 for 8-byte scalars). Method: SHMEM-send self-guard: a signalled %shmem-send hard fault -> UDP fallback + counter + sender-error hook; the fault-vs-lane-full distinction (WP-SHMEM-SEND-SELF-GUARD, ADR 0013)
Notes: WP-SHMEM-SEND-SELF-GUARD DONE 2026-06-18 (ADR 0013 SHMEM-send-self-guard note; standard DDS, NOT R6). A SIGNALED %shmem-send hard fault (segment detached / pshared / bounds) is caught in %send-raw-buf (dds.disc), bumps disc-node-shmem-send-faults, fires *sender-emit-error-hook* (context :shmem-send-fault, via %note-shmem-send-fault, ignore-errors-guarded), and falls back to UDP exactly like a return-0 -> the datagram still delivers (a genuinely lost reliable sample repairs via HEARTBEAT/ACKNACK, RTPS 2.5 §8.4 / §8.4.1). The catch lives in dds.disc (not the dds.xport SHMEM :send lambda) so the counter + hook stay in scope with NO upward dds.xport->dds.disc dependency; the :send lambda stays unguarded so it can signal up. FAULT-VS-LANE-FULL: the handler-case fires ONLY on a SIGNAL; a benign lane-full (the SHMEM send RETURNS 0) takes the SILENT UDP fallback with NO counter bump / NO hook fire. Local send-error handling is implementation-defined (no RTPS clause); the UDP-fallback delivery is MORE conformant than a drop. Test affordance dds.xport.shmem:*debug-shmem-send-fault* (special, default NIL, exported) injects shmem-send-test-fault at the top of %shmem-send; NIL = byte-identical production, never wire-triggered (NFR-SEC-POSTURE). TESTS (green SBCL+Clasp): run-shmem-send-self-guard-test (arm the injector -> the reader STILL receives via UDP fallback + disc-node-shmem-send-faults advanced + hook fired :shmem-send-fault + disc-node-shmem-sends did NOT advance), run-shmem-send-self-guard-no-regression-test (injector NIL -> SHMEM still delivers, counter 0, hook silent; PLUS an all-UDP shmem-dest-NIL send unaffected — that leg on BOTH impls). The SHMEM legs pass-skip on the Clasp/macOS by-name-attach gap (ADR 0013). Off the measured CDR hot path — make mem 0.0000 serialize/deserialize/round-trip, no hot-path number moved, no bench warranted (FR-LANG-7). 250 green SBCL+Clasp; gate-types(1324)+gate-hotpath(8 files)+mem(0.0000)+fuzz PASS.

Notes: WP-SHMEM-SEND-SELF-GUARD cross-DDS DoD (owner directive 2026-06-17). Method: TRANSIENT durability service Phase 1+2 (embedded entity): pluggable store, multi-service runner, OTP supervisor, CLI/env entrypoint, thread-or-process; Phase 2: dedup/no-double-delivery, multi-topic, dispose/unregister, foreign-service coexistence

Phase 2 WP-DURABILITY-DEDUP: (1) NO-DOUBLE-DELIVERY via PID_ORIGINAL_WRITER_INFO (0x0061, RTPS 2.5 §8.3.5.4) — relay writer tags each relayed DATA with the original writer GUID + SN as inline-QoS; receiver-side dedup uses a per-origGUID contiguous watermark + bounded reorder set (ADR 0024); false-reject impossible (watermark starts at 0 for a new GUID, so low late-joiner replay SNs are accepted even after high live SNs); (2) MULTI-TOPIC — N disc-nodes per service-start, one per topic, isolated store partitions; (3) DISPOSE/UNREGISTER CAPTURE + REPLAY — lifecycle events stored as :disposed/:unregistered durable-records and replayed carrying PID_ORIGINAL_WRITER_INFO; (4) FOREIGN-SERVICE COEXISTENCE MECHANISM — receiver-side dedup on the shared originalGUID+SN gives exactly-once when multiple relays carry the same sample (our-stack-proven by run-durability-no-double-delivery-test), and our service announces itself a persistence relay (vendor PID_SERVICE_KIND) so a foreign service/Connext recognizes it; the LIVE dual-relay proof vs RTI PS is CLOSED_WITH_FINDINGS — RTI PS does NOT relay TRANSIENT_LOCAL (only TRANSIENT/PERSISTENT), so a TL-tier dual-relay run is not exercisable, deferred to Phase 3 (see interop/durability-dedup/coexistence/). FUZZ: PID-parse fuzz arm in pbt-test.lisp (parse-original-writer-info + parse-inline-qos-key-status, 2000 iters each, BOTH arms prod + safety-0; NFR-SEC-POSTURE). Remaining (Phase 3): in-memory only (disk + CNSA-2.0 DARE deferred); dynamic topic-add deferred; dedup-map prune for stale GUIDs deferred; Leg C post-Task-8 live re-run CLOSED_WITH_FINDINGS: RTI PS v7.3.1 does NOT relay TRANSIENT_LOCAL (it only handles TRANSIENT/PERSISTENT); our service relayed correctly; dual-relay coexistence live proof requires TRANSIENT topic (Phase 3 deferred).

Method: Always-on CNSA-2.0 Data-At-Rest Encryption over the durability store (ADR 0021 cap.7): KEM-DEM envelope (ML-KEM-1024 -> HKDF-SHA384 DEK -> per-store AES-256-GCM, counter nonce, AAD-bound metadata, fail-closed), pluggable key-provider/KMS hook, all-secrets foreign/static, OpenSSL >= 3.5 native crypto (no hand-rolling, FR-SEC-2), bounds-checked + fuzzed open path, cross-DDS wire transparency
Notes: WP-DURABILITY-DARE Phase 3a (ADR 0025). NEW dds-dare ASDF system + a thin encrypted-store decorator in dds-durability. ENVELOPE: per-store ML-KEM-1024 (FIPS-203) encapsulate -> HKDF-SHA384 DEK (RFC 5869, info='dds-dare/dek/v1') -> AES-256-GCM (SP 800-38D) per record with a 96-bit COUNTER nonce; AAD = topic || writer-guid(16) || sn(8 LE) || kind(1) (authenticated cleartext so the inner store indexes/replays); on-store bytes = version(1) || nonce(12) || ciphertext || tag(16). NIST/IETF KATs (the conformance oracle, PUBLISHED sources, NEVER self-generated): AES-256-GCM vs NIST SP 800-38D Test Case 16 (run-dare-aes-gcm-kat-test); SHA-384 vs FIPS-180-4 + HKDF-SHA384 vs RFC 5869 (run-dare-sha384-hkdf-kat-test); ML-KEM-1024 vs C2SP/CCTV vectors (run-dare-ml-kem-kat-test). Envelope round-trip + AAD + tamper + wrong-key (run-dare-envelope-test); decorator seal/unseal byte-exact + tamper-drop + delegate (run-dare-encrypted-store-test, run-dare-encrypted-store-lifecycle-test). CRYPTO LIB: OpenSSL >= 3.5 (3.6.2 on this host) via HANDLE-BASED CFFI (cffi:foreign-symbol-pointer on an explicitly-resolved *libcrypto* handle — fixes a LibreSSL global-namespace collision that broke Clasp; impl-agnostic, NO reader conditionals), no primitive hand-rolled (FR-SEC-2; libsodium NOT used — lacks ML-KEM + SHA-384). FAIL-CLOSED everywhere: open-payload returns NIL (never plaintext) on short/wrong-version/auth-fail blob; get-range DROPS a failed record + fires *dare-error-hook*; OpenSSL<3.5 / ML-KEM-absent -> hard startup error (dare-available-p), NEVER a plaintext fallback. SECRET HANDLING (owner 'all secrets' directive, conformance): the ML-KEM private key, the shared secret, AND the DEK live in foreign-backed static-vectors (zeroized + freed via free-secret-octets at end-of-life); the DEK is BORN in a static-vector (never transits the heap); secret frees unwind-protect-guarded (throw-safe). KEY-PROVIDER: pluggable closure-vtable (the KMS hook) + default file provider (ML-KEM-1024 keypair, perms enforced 0600/0700 + checked at open, fail-CLOSED on loose OR unverifiable perms, internal decapsulate so the raw private key never leaves the provider); run-dare-key-provider-test. OPEN-PATH FUZZ (NFR-SEC-POSTURE; the operating contract §4): fuzz-dare-open-payload (pbt-test.lisp, 3000 iters) feeds open-payload adversarial sealed blobs (short/oversized/random/all-zero/tampered/wrong-AAD/strictly-truncated-valid + a genuinely-sealed blob under its true AAD) -> NIL or the CORRECT plaintext, NEVER an error/OOB/crash; a (safety 0) arm reaches the same verdict (the bounds guards are explicit manual checks, safety-independent); SKIPs cleanly if OpenSSL<3.5 (the KATs then carry crypto correctness). CROSS-DDS TRANSPARENCY (per-feature DoD, light by nature — DARE adds ZERO wire surface): in-process authoritative proof run-dare-service-transparency-test (a DARE-wrapped service delivers byte-correct retained samples to a same-stack late-joiner; SBCL + Clasp, Clasp first). LIVE foreign-peer confirmation (interop/durability-dare/, 2026-06-19, BOTH peers): a DARE-wrapped durability service delivered byte-correct samples to LIVE TL late-joiners — CONNEXT 7.3.1 received 352 (service retained 403), FAST DDS 3.6.1 received 152 (= 152 collected) — and both captures match the plain-store transient wire BYTE-FOR-BYTE (replay EntityId 0x00000102, firstAvailableSeqNumber=1 held on every HEARTBEAT, CDR_LE (0x0001) on all DATA, NACK->retransmit). NFR-MEM: make mem stays 0.0000 (DARE is control-plane, off the measured CDR hot path) -> no bench. Producers wipe transient heap secrets after the static copy. MINOR-4 open follow-on: all-kms grows monotonically (remote-participant KMs held+zeroized at teardown, not dropped/wiped on unmatch).

CRYPTO CONFIRMED SOUND (full investigation, NOT touched): epoch-id = monotonic persisted counter max+1 (store-encrypted.lisp:736, not time-based), DEK = HKDF of a FRESH ML-KEM encapsulation per epoch (:739-742, not HKDF(epoch-id)), nonce = per-epoch counter reset-0 then ++ (:749/776); (DEK,nonce) reuse is IMPOSSIBLE incl fast restart -- NO nonce-reuse vulnerability. FIX: dedup the captured OWI hits by (GUID,SN) and assert exactly N DISTINCT PIDs, every distinct GUID == the publisher, and the distinct SN set == {1..N} -- retransmit-insensitive and STRICTLY STRONGER than the old in-range check; test-only (the *datagram-sink* global and the reliable-TL retransmit are correct product behaviour, not a defect). Notes: WP-DURABILITY-EPOCHS-MAC (ADR 0045 §7.2, 2026-07-07). Closes the last ADR-0045 §7 tamper-evidence residual: DIR/epochs.dat (the DARE per-epoch KEM-ciphertext table) was entry-CRC-only; the CRC is UNKEYED, so an offline disk adversary could flip a stored kem-ct AND recompute its per-entry CRC -> undetected -> wrong shared-secret -> wrong DEK -> fail-closed decrypt-failure (an availability brick / tamper-evidence gap); rollback + reorder likewise unauthenticated. FIX: a keyed HMAC over epochs.dat. k_epochs = HKDF-SHA384(ss, info=dds-dare/epochs/v1) is the THIRD sibling off the anchor shared secret (alongside the log-MAC key + k_meta) — it CANNOT derive from a per-epoch DEK (the DEKs ARE the contents of epochs.dat, circular), so %mint-logmac-anchor/%load-logmac-anchor derive+return all three keys from the same ss (freed on every path). Canonical signed image version||count||[%frame-epoch-entry]* over the entries SORTED BY EPOCH-ID ASCENDING (deterministic; reuses %frame-epoch-entry so each entry is byte-identical to on-disk), MAC'd HMAC-SHA-256(k_epochs, dds-dare/logmac/epochs/v1 || signed) (the same %hmac-labeled construction as the grandfather/tail anchors, a fresh label, NO new crypto) into a SEPARATE MUTABLE DIR/epochs.mac (signed||mac(32)||crc32(4), fsynced via the shared %write-anchor-file; %read-epochs-mac bounds-checks EVERY offset even at (safety 0)). SEAL at clean close (%seal-epochs-mac, right after the tail-anchor seal, before the keys free); VERIFY at open (%verify-epochs-mac, AFTER %load-epoch-deks' torn-tail truncate-recovery, guarded on k_epochs non-NIL) by PREFIX-CONTAINMENT, forward-tolerant: absent->CLEAN; .mac MAC mismatch->fail-closed; count<N->:truncated; first-N canonical image != stored signed->:diverged; a table with >=N whose first-N match->CLEAN (the extra is a forward 1-ahead crash-append; a strict whole-table-equality check would BRICK it and is REJECTED). NO invalidate-at-open (unlike §7.1): epochs.dat is append-only + never authorized-shrinks, so the only at-open divergence is the forward crash-append -> simpler than the tail anchor. Test-only *durability-debug-skip-epochs-seal* (mirrors *durability-debug-skip-tail-seal*, inert by default) exercises the no-false-reject path. 1 new test run-durability-epochs-mac-test (7 arms): (a) tamper-ct RED->GREEN headline [flip a kem-ct + recompute its per-entry CRC -> the unkeyed CRC path STILL accepts it (%load-epoch-table loads clean) but the keyed epochs.mac catches it :diverged fail-closed; non-vacuous clean control]; (b) rollback/truncation DETECTED :truncated + a forward-append CONTROL; (c) reorder DETECTED :diverged [swap the two kem-ct payloads + fix both per-entry CRCs -> the id<->ct binding differs from the sealed canonical image]; (d) epochs.mac-forge DETECTED [flip a byte in epochs.mac's own MAC + fix its CRC]; (e) cross-restart CLEAN; (f) 1-ahead crash-append CLEAN [the load-bearing no-false-reject]; (g) torn-tail CRC-recovery still verifies. Arms (a)-(d) assert the EXACT fail path via the condition report text (:diverged / :truncated / the epochs.mac self-MAC-mismatch wording) — botched byte-surgery cannot pass via a different error path. Residuals: the UNSEALED SUFFIX (epochs minted after the last clean close are unauthenticated until the next re-seal — the seal-at-close complement of forward-tolerance; damage bounded to fail-closed decrypt-failures of suffix-epoch records, never plaintext) + whole-file DELETION of epochs.dat/epochs.mac (the shared deletion residual, same class as anchor/tail deletion; sharpest form = laundering: delete epochs.mac + tamper + let the next clean close re-seal over the tampered table); torn-reseal recovery documented (:supersede in-place rewrite -> an OS crash mid-reseal leaves a torn epochs.mac that fail-louds at open until manually DELETED; absent -> clean, running-chain protection only); forward requirement recorded binding the epoch-table-retirement follow-on (retirement IS an authorized shrink -> that WP MUST rework the seal, e.g. invalidate-before-shrink + re-seal). Nonce-reuse confidentiality NOT at risk (each mint encapsulates a FRESH ciphertext even on id reuse) — integrity/availability + tamper-evidence-completeness, not confidentiality. Method: Type-gate false-REJECT fix (ADR 0057): a model parsed from a peer's LEGACY PID_TYPE_OBJECT_LB is assessed by ASSIGNABILITY with ALL bounds ignored — sequence, string, AND the XTypes §7.2.4.4.8 KEY sub-bound — and can NEVER be rejected on a bound. A legacy TypeObject is not a faithful encoding of the peer's declared type: rtiddsgen silently bounds an unbounded string at 255 (ADR 0009), so a stock Connext peer whose IDL says @key string color announces a 255-bounded KEY. The gate previously judged a remote READER under the §7.6.3.4.1 assumed DISALLOW_TYPE_COERCION (i.e. by struct EQUIVALENCE) and enforced the key sub-bound rule, both of which compare that invented bound — so it rejected a peer using the very same type, blocking EVERY DCPS DataWriter from matching EVERY stock vendor DataReader. New assignability-options ignore-key-bounds (default NIL = the spec rule; set ONLY by the legacy rung). The gate is not disarmed: extensibility, member count, ids, names, kinds, key FLAGS and must_understand still reject as before. Consequence recorded: against a legacy-only peer an explicit local DISALLOW_TYPE_COERCION cannot be honoured soundly and is downgraded (logged).

Method: ADR 0058 — the ZC/SHMEM in-slot data_protection SecuredPayload overlay (ADR 0051) now serves the SIGN tier as well as ENCRYPT, so a SIGN-only wire-protected writer regains Zero-Copy instead of being gated off. %zc-overlay-eligible-p no longer demands key-material-encrypt-p; an AES256-GMAC EntityCrypto KM seals a GMAC SecuredPayload into the slot — the payload stays VISIBLE (as the SIGN tier leaves it visible on the wire) and is AUTHENTICATED by a common_mac the reader verifies fail-closed. The alternative ADR 0051 originally sketched (relax SIGN to RAW ZC, no overlay) is REJECTED: the RTPS signature covers only the 20-octet reference datagram, so a raw slot payload would be UNAUTHENTICATED — a co-resident process could tamper with the sample undetected, silently dropping the integrity guarantee the SIGN tier exists to provide. Gate relaxation only, NOT new crypto: encode-serialized-payload-into already implements both §9.5.3.3 sub-tiers and the reader's decode is gated on the overlay sentinel, not the tier. Carried with it: the send-side slot-capacity gate now uses the EXACT per-tier sealed length (new dds.security:secured-payload-length — ENCRYPT 44+N+pad4(N), SIGN 40+align4(N)) instead of a hardcoded ENCRYPT-only 44+len+3, so it can neither under-count (overflow) nor needlessly refuse a payload that would have fit. The single-shared-KM nonce invariant (ADR 0051 Forward Requirement) still governs: GMAC is AES-GCM with an empty plaintext and consumes the SAME iv-counter, so a second KM copy would reintroduce (key,nonce) reuse for SIGN exactly as for ENCRYPT. ALSO: ADR 0051 deferred follow-on 2 (-into-sap direct seal) is CLOSED as DECLINED on measurement.

Method: ADR 0059 — discharge the four recorded FORWARD REQUIREMENTS (hazards unreachable today by a structural accident, with an instruction that a future WP must handle them). (1) %km-session-key-at two-slot publish (ADR 0038(a)/0039(d)): THE PREMISE WAS FALSE — the decode receiver is NOT single-threaded (start-node runs up to THREE receiver threads: unicast UDP + multicast UDP + SHMEM, all feeding %handle-datagram, able to decode from the SAME peer under the SAME participant KM) and session_id is read OFF THE WIRE, so a concurrent-different-session_id tear (KM advertising id S1 alongside key(S2) -> a later hit returns the WRONG key) was REACHABLE TODAY with no rekeying feature at all; fail-closed (a wrong key cannot forge a GCM tag -> the datagram drops) hence unnoticed, and safe only by the ACCIDENT that conformant peers use a fixed session_id. FIXED BY CONSTRUCTION: the discriminant + key are now ONE immutable session-cache object published by a SINGLE store (both the send-side cache and the receiver-specific origin-auth cache, whose discriminant is FOUR fields), so a reader sees the old pair or the new pair, never a mix. (2) ADR 0031 lim.1 decode-fail counters: DISCHARGED — each writer's counter table is STAMPED with the KM sender_key_id and RESET on change, so a future rotation cannot suppress samples encoded under the NEW key. (3) ADR 0043 reader-arming window: made FAIL-SAFE — the HEARTBEAT gate now requires the reader-side durability baseline to be ARMED as well as matched; a matched-but-unarmed HEARTBEAT is DROPPED + COUNTED (disc-node-hb-unarmed-drops, which MUST stay 0), so a WP that reopens the window pays one HEARTBEAT period of latency instead of shipping a silent DURABILITY violation. (4) ADR 0045 §7.2 epochs seal: cannot be discharged early (the seal deliberately cannot distinguish an authorized shrink from rollback tampering), so the :truncated ERROR now names its own obligation to the epoch-table-retirement WP.

Notes: Test km-session-cache-tear (new): hammers one KM from 4 threads x 6 interleaved DISTINCT session_ids and asserts (a) every lookup returns the key of the session_id it ASKED FOR and (b) every published cache object is SELF-CONSISTENT (its key is exactly what its own id derives) — for BOTH caches incl. the four-field origin-auth discriminant. The existing repair-delivered test caught a WRONG first form of the ADR 0043 guard ('matched => proxy must exist'), which would have dropped EVERY HEARTBEAT on the bare-disc path (the low-level tests + the shapes runners never arm a baseline by design) — the guard is therefore conditioned on disc-node-durability-gate-active, set by the DCPS create-datareader. HOT-PATH BENCH (bench/report/2026-07-11-km-session-cache-single-object.md): the session-key cache HIT goes 6.6 -> 7.8 ns/op (one extra indirection) = 0.16% of the ~750 ns AEAD call it feeds; the end-to-end 256B seal is unchanged within noise (752.1 -> 749.1 ns). Method: ADR 0060 — (1) DDS 1.4 §2.2.2.1.1.7 'a disabled entity does not communicate': a DataWriter/DataReader created DISABLED (its factory's ENTITY_FACTORY autoenable_created_entities is FALSE) is now WITHHELD from the wire — the disc node keeps a registered-but-not-yet-enabled EntityId set; announce-endpoints does not SEDP-announce them (plain AND secure SEDP — the filter runs before the discovery-protection split) and %match-remote-endpoint does not match them, so an inbound remote cannot bind to a disabled endpoint either; enable() calls enable-local-endpoint, which RELEASES it (the next announce advertises it, it matches, data flows). Registration stays EAGER (ADR 0052's reason holds: the engine EntityId is assigned at create); only VISIBILITY changed. Default autoenable path -> the table is empty -> announce/match sets are byte-identical. WHY IT WAS BROKEN: ADR 0052 §3 deferred true deferred-registration arguing 'discovery is spin-driven, so a disabled endpoint that is never spun never announces' — already thin (an app spinning for its OTHER endpoints announces the disabled one too) and KILLED OUTRIGHT by S7's autonomous announcer (ADR 0056): the participant now spins ITSELF. Measured before the fix: two autonomous participants each holding a DISABLED endpoint MATCHED anyway (matched=1 both sides). Lesson recorded in the ADR: a deferral justified by 'nothing currently exercises this path' is only as durable as the reason nothing exercises it. (2) ADR 0054's v1 non-trigger CLOSED: reader-suppress-sn (a permanently-undecodable secured SN, ADR 0031 lim.1) now raises SAMPLE_LOST — suppression stops the reader NACKing the SN, so no retransmit can EVER recover it; not counting it meant a real irrecoverable loss reached the application with NO status (SAMPLE_LOST.total_count stayed 0 while the sample simply never arrived, which is exactly what DDS 1.4 §2.2.4.1 defines SAMPLE_LOST for). Fired via the same hook + route fan-out as the irrecoverable-GAP path, OUTSIDE the node lock.
Notes: Test dcps-disabled-endpoint-silent (new, RED before): two AUTONOMOUS participants each holding a DISABLED endpoint do NOT match after 2.5 s of announcing (RED: matched=1 both sides), and enable() then RELEASES them — they match and a sample flows end-to-end (the fix WITHHOLDS, it does not strand). Test decode-fail-suppress (extended): the arm that trips suppression now also asserts SAMPLE_LOST fires on the matched DataReader (RED before: the loss was silent). ALSO CLOSED WITHOUT CODE, honestly: the ADR 0052 §3 node-scoped-pool deferral is BY DESIGN (the ZC/secured pools + per-node arenas are SHARED across a participant's N endpoints per ADR 0048, so deleting one of N must not tear down a pool a sibling still uses — bounded by the participant lifetime, not a leak, not a UAF), and the file backend's topics.map-loss cross-restart non-reclaim is benign + SQLite-immune. 562/562 both impls, gate-hotpath + gate-types green; no wire-format change, no hot-path change.

Method: ADR 0081 slice 3 — same-host detection against RTI Connext shared memory, by RTI's own published test (transport_shmem.h:89-96): attach read-only to the System V segment keyed 0x400000+RTPS-port and compare its shmemUUID against the 12 octets in the peer's advertised Locator_t. There is no locator-only way to decide co-location; RTI's header states the test requires reading the segment.
Notes: Segment layout MEASURED, not published — established by controlled variation (a documented Connext QoS property set to a distinctive value, then the segment diffed), so each offset is identified by a chosen value appearing where predicted: receive_buffer_size @0x58 (set 777216, read 777216), message_size_max @0x5c (set 20480, read 20480), received_message_count_max @0x60 (set 37, read 37). shmemUUID @0x24 PROVEN byte-identical to the same participant's SPDP-advertised locator address, measured simultaneously. Addressing CORRECTED from the slice-1 record: segment key is 0x400000+port (NOT 0x800000); semaphore 0x800000+port; mutex 0xB00000+port — confirmed by the header field order (transport_shmem.h:50-66 vs the :194-199 initialiser), by live ipcs, and by predicting the keys for six domains before starting a peer on each. NEW PAL surface sysv-shm-attach-readonly/-create/-detach/-destroy/-sap, one CFFI implementation serving SBCL and Clasp, no reader conditionals (gate-pal green); least-bytes IS the bounds check and the KERNEL enforces it (shmget returns EINVAL when the segment is shorter than requested), which is why no shmctl(IPC_STAT) wrapper exists — struct shmid_ds differs between Darwin and Linux. SHM_RDONLY/IPC_CREAT/IPC_EXCL/IPC_RMID read from sys/shm.h+sys/ipc.h on BOTH platforms, identical. Returns FOUR outcomes, not a boolean: (T NIL) same host; (NIL NIL) well-formed but another host (ordinary, NOT an error); (NIL :no-such-segment); (NIL :not-an-rti-shmem-segment); (NIL :unvalidated-shmem-protocol-version) — an RTI segment of a revision this layout was not measured against is REFUSED, never parsed (RTI names five revisions and specifies none). TEST run-rti-shmem-recognition-test builds its own synthetic segment (no Connext needed) and drives all five outcomes; FALSIFIED BOTH WAYS — deleting the majorVersion refusal makes an unmeasured revision report T (a confident wrong answer), and short-circuiting the UUID comparison makes a foreign host report T. LIVE-VALIDATED against a running Connext 7.3.1 shapes_pub on domain 0: T at its metatraffic port 7412 AND its user port 7413; wrong UUID at that same live port -> (NIL NIL); real UUID at a port with no segment -> (NIL :no-such-segment). 578/578 SBCL and Clasp; gate-build PASS both (clean cache, self-falsified), gate-types/gate-hotpath/gate-nocond(0)/gate-pal green. SCOPE LIMIT: measured on macOS/arm64 only, Connext 7.3.1, shmem protocol majorVersion 2 — Linux/CI is the oracle for anything platform-shaped and the SysV surface is exactly that; re-measure there. Read-only throughout: nothing writes to a Connext-owned segment.

Method: ADR 0081 slice 4 — read an RTI Connext receiver's embedded shared-memory transport properties and bound what may be written to it. RTI documents that a receiver's properties are embedded in its segment and that a SENDER verifies compatibility before use, so this is a prerequisite for slices 6-7.
Notes: rti-shmem-segment-properties returns segment-size + receive_buffer_size (0x58) + message_size_max (0x5c) + received_message_count_max (0x60); rti-shmem-datagram-fits-p bounds a datagram by message_size_max — the shared-memory analogue of the ADR 0079 emitted-datagram-size interop contract. EVERY LENGTH IS CORROBORATED BEFORE IT IS BELIEVED: the size the segment states about ITSELF is a number written by another process, so the segment is re-attached at that claimed size and the KERNEL decides (shmget refuses a request larger than the segment) — a segment overstating its extent is refused with :implausible-segment-properties instead of becoming a bound that later sizes a buffer. Remaining plausibility checks are PHYSICAL, never policy (a buffer cannot exceed the segment holding it, all fields non-zero), deliberately NOT an invented ceiling, because false-REJECT of a conformant peer is the worst failure class (OMG-conformance directive) and a peer may legitimately configure any message_size_max its segment accommodates. Header magic + majorVersion checks factored into %rti-shmem-header-status so the co-location test and the property reader can never diverge on whether a segment may be interpreted. TEST run-rti-shmem-properties-test builds its own synthetic segment (no Connext needed): exact read-back of all four fields; the fits/does-not-fit boundary at message_size_max and message_size_max+1; and three refusals — a segment CLAIMING twice its real extent, a receive_buffer_size beyond the segment, and a zero message_size_max. FALSIFIED: removing the kernel corroboration makes the overstating segment ACCEPTED, returning a properties struct carrying the lie (segment-size 8192 from a 4096-byte segment). LIVE-VALIDATED against a running Connext 7.3.1 shapes_pub on domain 0 ports 7412 AND 7413: segment=1115312 (matches ipcs segsz exactly), receive_buffer_size=1048576, message_size_max=65536, received_message_count_max=64 — all three EQUAL RTI's own published defaults (RECEIVE_BUFFER_SIZE_DEFAULT = message_size_max/4*count = 65536/4*64 = 1048576; MESSAGE_SIZE_MAX_DEFAULT 65536; RECEIVED_MESSAGE_COUNT_MAX_DEFAULT 64), and a 65536-octet datagram fits while 65537 does not. 579/579 SBCL and Clasp; gate-build PASS both (clean cache, self-falsified), gate-types/gate-hotpath/gate-nocond(0)/gate-pal green. Read-only throughout. SCOPE LIMIT: same as slice 3 — layout measured on macOS/arm64, Connext 7.3.1, majorVersion 2; no Connext exists on the Linux box so the layout leg cannot be re-measured there.

Method: ADR 0081 slice 7a — write a record into an RTI Connext receiver's shared-memory ring by the measured producer protocol, and wake it. First transmit into an RTI segment; foundation for full SHMEM interop transmit (7b live).
Notes: New System V SEMAPHORE PAL surface (sysv-sem-open/-create/-op/-setval/-getval/-destroy) + sysv-shm-attach-readwrite, one CFFI implementation for SBCL and Clasp; SETVAL/GETVAL command numbers differ per OS (Darwin 8/5, Linux 16/12 — the ONLY reader conditional; SEM_UNDO 0x1000 identical) — all read from sys/sem.h on both, SETVAL=8 cross-checked against a live Connext semctl via dtrace. rti-shmem-write-record follows the protocol measured in ADR 0081 §5.0 (traced directly): take the ring mutex with SEM_UNDO (so a crash cannot deadlock RTI's receiver), write the record at the producer cursor and advance it by align8(len), write the FULL producer control state (block A head + block B tail positions & counters + the (-datagram_length,0) descriptor entry — the write-set measured in ADR 0081 §5.0 by stopping the consumer), release, then raise the data flag with semctl SETVAL 1 (idempotent — the wake RTI uses, NOT semop(+1)). The mutex serialises writers; the consumer is lockless (matching our own reader). Bounded by message_size_max (:datagram-too-large) and the ring end. TEST run-rti-shmem-write-roundtrip-test builds a real RTI-shaped receiver (segment + mutex set resting 1 + data set resting 0) and proves write/read are inverses through real System V objects — TWO records so the advance is exercised, data flag confirmed raised to 1, mutex confirmed back to 1, oversized refused. FALSIFIED two ways: remove the SETVAL wake -> flag-raised assert fails; drop the cursor advance -> record B fails to read back. GATED on dds.pal:sysv-sem-setval-reliable-p (a runtime probe: create a private set, SETVAL 42, GETVAL, require 42): on Clasp/macOS-arm64 semctl's variadic value mispasses (ADR 0013, same NFR-PORT gap as shm_open) so SETVAL cannot wake the peer and the writer REFUSES with :setval-unavailable rather than landing an un-signalled record; the Clasp/macOS suite asserts that refusal. 582/582 SBCL and Clasp on macOS; 582/582 SBCL on Linux where SETVAL and SEM_UNDO were both confirmed to work (register varargs). gate-build PASS both impls (clean cache, self-falsified), gate-types/gate-hotpath/gate-nocond(0)/gate-pal green. SCOPE: framing (align8) and descriptor length (-D) are BOTH validated against a live peer (5 payloads); the full producer write-set is measured and written. Slice 7b LIVE (writing into a running Connext ring) is DEFERRED — two facts (descriptor slot index, initial counter relationship) stay unvalidated against a live peer, and a live write corrupts rather than misreads if wrong, so it awaits a sandboxed test vs a THROWAWAY participant. Read-write attach is used ONLY on the transmit path, bracketed by the ring mutex; everything else stays read-only.
